messages:
maria: quick design question — we're finalizing the envelope strategy for multi-tenant blobs. main constraints: per-tenant key separation, KMS call budget (AWS/GCP/Azure have different QPS), and audit fields for compliance. thoughts?
aj: curious — are we planning to keep DEKs in-memory cache on s3-upload workers, or persist wrapped DEK in DB per-object?
maria: plan was to persist wrapped DEK in metadata (per-object) and allow short-lived in-memory DEK cache on workers to avoid constant unwrap calls. want to confirm TTL and RBAC surface.
kevin: for RBAC, we should separate wrap/unwrap privileges from management. service accounts that call KMS to unwrap should have only kms:Decrypt or equivalent; key admin perms (rotate/disable) stay with platform-admins group. also need resource-level constraints so tenant A can't call wrap with tenant B's KEK.
samira: +1. For GCP we can use CMEK key rings with IAM bindings at key-level. Azure Key Vault supports RBAC policies and soft-delete. But watch the difference: GCP allows grantee on key, AWS uses grants or key policy. Ops needs a mapping layer that enforces tenant-to-key binding.
irene: audit logging requirements from compliance: every unwrap/rotate/disable must emit structured audit event with: actor, service_account, tenant_id, key_id, operation (wrap/unwrap/rotate), request_id, object_id, region, success/failure, latency_ms. retention 7y for regulated customers.
maria: good — can we surface those events into our existing audit log pipeline (kinesis -> longterm store)? any size/cost concerns?
kevin: volume check: typical unwrap rate per object create = 1 unwrap. For high-throughput ingest (10k/s) we can't hit KMS 10k/s. caching helps: keep DEK cache with per-tenant LRU + max TTL. propose default in-memory DEK TTL 30s and a leaky-bucket QPS cap per service account. also fallback to async rewrap?
aj: 30s sounds short for heavy loads. What if a worker pool is ephemeral — cache miss storms on scale-up. Maybe allow a warmup phase: prefetch DEKs on instance start for tenants present in batch. and an adaptive TTL: base 60s, backoff to 10s if memory pressure.
samira: cost/latency tradeoff: AWS KMS latency ~10-50ms/unlock, GCP similar, Azure slightly higher. Batching unwrap doesn't work because unwraps are per DEK. We should support a local wrapped-DEK cache that stores the ciphertext DEK (wrapped blob) + last_unwrap_time and optionally plaintext DEK in memory with a ttl. store wrapped blob always in DB so rebuild on restart.
kevin: security consideration: if someone obtains worker memory snapshot, plaintext DEK exposure window = TTL. so limit TTL and encrypt process memory? also ensure creds for the worker have tightly scoped STS tokens and short lifetime. add detection rule: if DEK unwrap rate for a single worker >> normal, alert (possible key exfil attempt).
maria: good point. For incident response, propose runbook steps: 1) revoke KEK (disable key) 2) push emergency rotation: generate new KEK and rewrap DEKs lazily on access 3) revoke affected service accounts and rotate app creds 4) audit-scan for objects unwrapped during compromise window 5) notify compliance. Any additions?
irene: add an isolation step — temporarily forbid unwrap for non-critical tenants to reduce blast radius. also capture a snapshot of KMS logs and grant ops read-only access for triage.
aj: about lazy rewrap: we need a tombstone in object metadata when its DEK is still wrapped with old KEK, and a background job that rewraps on read/write. also ensure we have idempotent rewrap logic.
kevin: one more: KMS call frequency limiter per-region and per-tenant. define soft QPS and hard QPS. soft breaches trigger sampling and incremental caching, hard breaches fallback to deny requests with 503 and degrade feature. we need SLA doc updates.
samira: audit visibility: include KMS request ids in our traces so we can tie a user action to a KMS unwrap. add a field in trace: kms_request_id and key_version.
maria: can someone draft concrete defaults for the config we ship? e.g. default plaintext_DEK_TTL=45s, cache_max_entries=1000 per node, per-tenant qps_soft=50, qps_hard=200, rewrap_batch_size=500 — and note provider differences.
kevin: I'll sketch defaults and provider caveats: AWS: use grants to reduce KMS API throttles, prefer KMS Multi-Region keys for cross-region failover. GCP: watch key ring IAM latency when changing perms. Azure: KeyVault has burst quotas.
aj: ops items: add metrics: kms_unwrap_count, kms_unwrap_errors, cache_hit_ratio, cache_evictions, unwrap_latency_p50/p95. alarms: unwrap_errors > 0.1% 5m, cache_hit_ratio < 60% 10m.
maria: thanks — can we also add a small example config block for teams so they can tune per workload? e.g.
```
# envelope config
plaintext_dek_ttl: 45s
cache_max_entries: 1000
per_tenant_qps_soft: 50
per_tenant_qps_hard: 200
rewrap_on_access: true
```
kevin: looks good. last thing: update RBAC docs and create a short runbook for key compromise drills (quarterly). i'll open a PR to the runbooks repo and a ticket for engineering to implement cache metrics + alarms.
kms-bot: deploy scheduled: kms-metrics-agent will rollout to staging at 03:00 UTC tomorrow.
oncall-bot: paging oncall: please review proposed rate limits and incident steps (link: https://go/runbooks/kms-envelope-draft) :bell:
maria: perfect — thanks everyone. I'll collect defaults and open the RFC today.
